assertions.assert: Without a database (the `<param>` `database` null, its default) it offers nothing on start and answers each `bot.ability.reflection.input` `{turn, cognition_input, cognition_output}` at once with `bot.ability.reflection.output` (no data), asking no model.

With a database, `recalling` reads the prior episodes and the behavior inventory in one memory transaction and `processing` asks the generate service (schema `dispatch`) to select at most one of `bot.behavior.create`, `bot.behavior.change` or `bot.behavior.break` (a change's and a break's `name` pinned to the inventory's names, and neither offered when the inventory is empty; decision D100); an empty selection goes to `storing`, which stores the turn's episode and answers `bot.ability.reflection.output`.

More than one selected event fails the turn with `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "Reflection select must return at most one behavior event."}`; a failed select call fails it with `Reflection select failed (<code>)`; a select call whose streamed reply makes no progress for `select_timeout_ms` (its first `generate.progress` arms it, each later one re-arms it) or that runs `select_ceiling_ms` in all fails it with `Reflection child cancellation timed out.` (decision D101).

A selected `bot.behavior.break` (`breaking`) marks the named behavior BROKEN with its trimmed reason and keeps the row, then stores the episode and answers `bot.ability.reflection.output`; a break of a name the inventory does not hold is not offered, so a model that selects one fails the select with `Reflection select failed (schema-mismatch)`.

A selected `bot.behavior.create` (`revising`) stores a DRAFT stub for a new name, invokes the builder bot with a `builder.request`, and on the builder's `done` (`accepting`) replaces the row ACTIVE with the built document, then stores the episode and answers `bot.ability.reflection.output`; a `bot.behavior.change` of a stored name revises it the same way, and a change of a name the inventory does not hold is not offered, so a model that selects one fails the select with `Reflection select failed (schema-mismatch)`.

A builder that fails with the last draft it rejected (`abandoning`) keeps that draft in the row as DRAFT and fails the turn with `Reflection change abandoned: same diagnostic message after fix:` and the rendered diagnostics (no-progress); a builder that fails with no draft fails the turn with `Reflection revision failed: <reason>: <first diagnostic>`, the create's DRAFT stub kept.

`revising` is bounded by `revising_timeout_ms` without progress while a builder generation streams (the builder, invoked with `progress_target` `'#_parent'`, passes on each `generate.progress` of its streamed generations, which arms it, and sends `builder.progress` as it enters a stage, which disarms it) and by `revising_ceiling_ms` in all (the `<param>` `bounds` overriding either, decision D101): when one passes, the revision is cancelled and the turn fails with `Reflection child cancellation timed out.`.

A memory transaction that fails (here the recall, on a database the run does not grant) fails the turn with `Reflection memory recall failed: <detail>`; after any failure the turn's episode is stored with no behavior (unless storing it is what failed; decision D97) and the reflection is idle again and takes the next input.
An input that arrives while a reflection is in hand waits and runs after it, in order: each turn gets its own answer.
